{{ElectionsOH}}
The '''2014 Ohio Secretary of State election''' was held on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[Ohio Secretary of State]], concurrently with elections to the [[2014 United States House of Representatives elections in Ohio|U.S. House of Representatives]], [[2014 Ohio gubernatorial election|governor]], and other [[2014 Ohio elections|state]] and [[2014 United States elections#Local elections|local]] elections. Primary elections were held on May 6, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 12, 2013 |title=Notice of Primary Election – May 6, 2014 |url=https://allen.boe.ohio.gov/2013/12/12/notice-of-primary-election-may-6-2014/ |access-date=October 21, 2025 |website=Allen County Board of Elections}}</ref>

Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] secretary [[Jon Husted]] ran for re-election to a second term in office.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kopan |first=Tal |date=February 12, 2014 |title=The state races ignored — until now |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2014/02/secretary-of-state-elections-2014-103425 |access-date=October 21, 2025 |website=POLITICO}}</ref> He defeated [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state senator [[Nina Turner]] in the general election.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 4, 2014 |title=GOP's Husted Re-Elected As Ohio Secretary Of State |url=https://www.wosu.org/news/2014-11-04/gops-husted-re-elected-as-ohio-secretary-of-state |access-date=October 21, 2025 |website=WOSU}}</ref> [[Electoral fraud in the United States|Voter fraud]], [[Redistricting in Ohio|redistricting]], and [[early voting]] were key issues during the campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Castele |first=Nick |date=September 24, 2014 |title=Conversations with the Candidates: Secretary of State Jon Husted and Nina Turner |url=https://www.ideastream.org/2014-09-24/conversations-with-the-candidates-secretary-of-state-jon-husted-and-nina-turner |access-date=October 21, 2025 |website=Ideastream Public Media}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Brand |first=Anna |date=August 13, 2014 |title=30 in 30: Women Candidates to Watch in 2014 -- Nina Turner |url=https://www.msnbc.com/msnbc/30-30-women-candidates-watch-2014-nina-turner-msna389706 |access-date=October 21, 2025 |website=MSNBC}}</ref> Turner conceded the race early on November 5.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farkas |first=Karen |date=November 5, 2014 |title=Nina Turner's campaign for secretary of state has ended, but she said her fight will continue |url=https://www.cleveland.com/open/2014/11/nina_turner_and_her_supporters.html |url-access=limited |access-date=October 21, 2025 |website=Cleveland.com |quote=Democratic Ohio Sen. Nina Turner announced she will not be the next secretary of state, but that is about all she conceded.}}</ref>
